official_sources.title: OGC Simple Feature Access Common Architecture
official_sources.finding: Simple Features defines common geometry architecture and spatial-reference association used by downstream validity and topological predicates.

official_sources.title: OGC Simple Feature Access SQL Option
official_sources.finding: Simple Feature Access SQL standardizes storage, retrieval and spatial query of simple feature collections and predicate semantics.

official_sources.title: GDAL Geometry Validity
official_sources.finding: GDAL warns invalid geometries can produce incorrect spatial-algorithm results; validity is based on Simple Features and GEOS.

official_sources.title: gdal vector check-geometry
official_sources.finding: Checks polygon validity and line simplicity, reports invalidity locations, and notes curved geometries are linearized before GEOS evaluation.

official_sources.title: gdal vector check-coverage
official_sources.finding: Coverage validity separately checks overlap, shared-edge node agreement and narrow gaps, assuming individual polygons are valid.

official_sources.title: OGRGeometry validity predicates and SetPrecision
official_sources.finding: OGR predicates do not themselves validate input; SetPrecision rounds to a grid while preserving valid topology, whereas simple coordinate rounding may create invalidity.

official_sources.title: gdal vector make-valid
official_sources.finding: Make-valid may use linework or structure algorithms and can change polygon structure or emit lower-dimensional components.

official_sources.title: ogr2ogr geometry precision controls
official_sources.finding: Coordinate-resolution changes invoke SetPrecision by default to avoid invalid output; skipping this protection or changing precision can alter geometry structure.

official_sources.title: PostGIS ST_IsValid
official_sources.finding: ST_IsValid tests OGC 2D validity and reports invalid geometries; higher dimensions do not change the 2D validity test.

official_sources.title: PostGIS ST_IsValidReason
official_sources.finding: ST_IsValidReason provides an auditable textual reason and location context for geometry invalidity such as self-intersection.

official_sources.title: PostGIS ST_MakeValid
official_sources.finding: MakeValid preserves input vertices where possible but can change a polygon into multipolygon or lower-dimensional collections after collapse.

official_sources.title: PostGIS ST_Contains
official_sources.finding: Contains requires common interior points; a polygon does not contain a point or line lying only on its boundary.

official_sources.title: PostGIS ST_Covers
official_sources.finding: Covers includes both interior and boundary and is therefore explicitly different from Contains for boundary-only points.

official_sources.title: PostGIS ST_CoveredBy
official_sources.finding: CoveredBy accepts geometry lying in the interior or boundary of the covering geometry and warns invalid inputs give unexpected results.

official_sources.title: PostGIS ST_Intersects
official_sources.finding: Intersects is true whenever geometries share any point and is expressible through DE-9IM matrix patterns.

official_sources.title: PostGIS ST_Relate DE-9IM
official_sources.finding: DE-9IM explicitly separates interior, boundary and exterior relationships and can serialize the exact topological relation used for membership decisions.

official_sources.title: PostGIS ST_SnapToGrid
official_sources.finding: SnapToGrid can remove consecutive collapsed points and may make returned geometry lose simplicity, so it is not a neutral formatting operation.

official_sources.title: GEOS GeometryPrecisionReducer
official_sources.finding: Topology-preserving precision reduction uses snap-rounding and can remove collapsed components; pointwise reduction may produce invalid polygonal geometry.

official_sources.title: GEOS precision namespace
official_sources.finding: GEOS distinguishes topology-preserving and non-topology-preserving precision reducers, exposing precision-model choice as part of provenance.

official_sources.title: GEOS MakeValid
official_sources.finding: GEOS MakeValid may change geometry type or dimension when invalid polygons collapse or self-intersect.

official_sources.title: GEOS CoverageValidator
official_sources.finding: Coverage validation can detect mismatched shared edges, overlaps and configured narrow gaps between polygons.

official_sources.title: gdal vector clean-coverage
official_sources.finding: Coverage cleaning alters boundaries to remove gaps and overlaps, so it is a derived repair operation that must never silently replace authoritative parcel geometry.
